transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-12
Start: 09:32 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (CTO, Vela), Daniel Cruz (Head of ML, Vela), Priya Menon (DevOps), Ethan Shaw (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Primary goal: discuss renewal timing, capacity uplift, and adding APAC region; evaluate Dedicated vs hosted options for compliance and latency; outline contract extension options (12 vs 24 mo) and next steps for procurement + technical bench.
- Action items: pricing, bench results, SOC2 + network diagram, peering contacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate the time. quick roll call?
[00:07] Asha (Vela): hey yeah this is Asha, and Daniel, Priya, Ethan are here.
[00:11] Daniel (Vela): hi all.
[00:13] Maya: awesome. goal for today, high level renewal / expansion roadmap — capacity bump, APAC region add, and contract term options. liam's gonna run through some infra notes and then we can go into procurement questions. sound good?
[00:24] Asha: perfect. we've come out of the pilot, usage has spiked month over month, so want to lock in predictable capacity and get APAC latency down.
[00:33] Liam (Redwood SE): yeah congrats on the pilot numbers — we saw the token patterns you shared. couple things up front: for APAC we usually recommend either Dedicated pools in the region or private edge; there's tradeoffs re: cost and warm-up.
[00:45] Priya (Vela): quick question — our SLO for user-facing latency is 250ms p95. does Redwood's hosted plan hit that from Singapore?
[00:53] Liam: so, short answer is sometimes; it depends on model and sequence length. for smaller models (<2k tokens) hosted in ap-southeast1 gets you close but not always under 250 p95 at peak. Dedicated in-region will give you a consistent envelope. we saw 140-180ms p95 on similar workloads for Dedicated. note: those numbers include our continuous batching, kv cache warm hits — if you have a lot of cold-starts the p95 spikes.
[01:20] Daniel: and the cost delta between hosted and Dedicated — ballpark?
[01:24] Maya: for your footprint, roughs were in the sheet we shared last quarter; Dedicated has a higher fixed monthly commit but unit costs go down and it's more predictable. we can model a blended approach: hosted for non-latency critical routes, Dedicated for auth/user-facing.
[01:39] Ethan (Vela Procurement): financially, we prefer predictable commitments. are there 12 vs 24 month discount levers?
[01:46] Maya: yes, 24-month gets an incremental discount and priority provisioning for new regions. we'll attach exact numbers in the pricing update.
[01:52] Priya: also open question — we need to keep logs for 13 months for audit. how does retention and data residency work with Redwood Private vs Hosted?
[02:01] Liam: hosted stores logs in region depending on your tenant region, but retention tiers are an add-on. Private (VPC/private deployment) gives you full control and you can configure retention to match 13 months easily. for SOC2 / ISO logs, we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding.
[02:20] Asha: good. security is a gating factor for the 24 month decision, so please share SOC2, encryption at rest details, and KMS story.
[02:28] Maya: sure, we'll drop the SOC2 pack and KMS integration notes.
[02:31] Liam: one thing to flag: if you're considering on-prem or VPC private deployment, there's a lead time to provision appliances and do network peering — typically 6-8 weeks plus a runbook handoff.
[02:44] Priya: 6-8 weeks is ok if we start in Feb. what's required from our side?
[02:48] Liam: network engineers for peering, firewall rules, and a small test cluster for early validation. we'll send a checklist.
[02:56] Daniel: can we run a throughput bench against your Dedicated nodes with our typical prompt mix? want to ensure tokens/sec meets our expectations.
[03:02] Liam: yes we can. action: I'll run a 24-hour throughput bench using your script and share graphs — that'll show steady-state throughput and tail latency.
[03:09] Maya: great, that will help procurement.
[03:11] Ethan: procurement question — if we upgrade mid-term, does pricing prorate?
[03:15] Maya: yes we do prorate capacity top-ups. contract amendments can cover uplifts.
[03:19] Asha: what's Redwood's fallback policy if a region suffers capacity pressure? e.g., APAC outage, do we get failover to hosted EU or US?
[03:28] Liam: we support smart routing/fallback — you can define policy to failover to a compatible model variant in another region; note that you'll see higher latency. also we support model pinning to prevent unintended downgrades during failovers.
[03:40] Priya: any limits on data egress or cross-region replication we should watch for?
[03:44] Liam: egress is standard cloud egress; for Private we can avoid cross-region replication unless you opt in. We'll include the network diagram for clarity.
[03:53] Daniel: curious about caching — our heavy users repeat similar prompts, can Redwood's prefix/K V cache reduce tokens?
[03:59] Liam: yes, prefix and kv cache can cut downstream tokens — we've seen 15-35% token reduction depending on prompt locality. caveat: not all prompts benefit.
[04:09] Asha: okay, moving to timeline — target: APAC go-live end of Q2, capacity uplift incremental starting Mar 1. is that realistic?
[04:18] Liam: technically yes if procurement and peering start early; key is contract signature and a quick pilot for Dedicated.
[04:25] Maya: procurement sign-off will trigger provisioning priority — 24-month term gets faster lane.
[04:29] Ethan: on the contract language — what's the SLA? uptime and latency SLOs?
[04:33] Maya: our standard Dedicated SLA is 99.95% uptime and latency SLOs are in the appendix per model class; we can append your p95 requirements for user-facing routes if you commit capacity.
[04:45] Priya: we need traceability for tokens for cost-allocation. does Redwood expose token breakdown per route or per api key?
[04:52] Liam: yes, Console has token-level breakdown, route-by-route dashboards, and you can tag requests. we'll show you a demo.
[04:58] Asha: can you also show canary rollout controls? we want canary for model upgrades.
[05:03] Liam: yep automatic canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback.
[05:07] Daniel: earlier you mentioned quantization recommendations — if we go Dedicated can we use quantized variants to save cost?
[05:12] Liam: we provide quantization profiles; some models can be served with INT8-like quantization with small quality delta. Redwood Optimize can recommend per-route quantization profiles.
[05:21] Maya: any competitive pressures? who else are you evaluating?
[05:24] Asha: mostly NimbusAI and a managed cloud provider CloudServe — their network presence in APAC is a bit better but Redwood's inference performance and tooling are compelling.
[05:34] Maya: noted. we think our unified runtime and rollout guarantees are a differentiator.
[05:38] Ethan: procurement process — we'll need security docs and an initial contract to our legal team. can you push those by Friday?
[05:44] Maya: yes we'll try for Friday (2026-01-16) with a pricing sheet.
[05:48] Priya: one last technical — if we enable prefix caching do we need to change SDKs?
[05:52] Liam: SDK changes minimal — mostly flags and cache window settings. we'll include sample config.
[05:58] Asha: ok let's recap next steps.
[06:01] Maya: recap: Maya send pricing + SOC2 + contract draft; Liam run bench and share network runbook and demo link; Priya to share peering contacts; Asha confirm budget owners. tentative follow-up in two weeks for Dedicated demo during working hours.
[06:17] Daniel: sounds good.
[06:20] Ethan: thanks all.
[06:22] Maya: thanks everyone — closing.
